claims.text: Dynamic formation or preservation of coherent nanoprecipitates in high-entropy alloys can simultaneously elevate yield strength and enhance ductility.
A homogeneous as-cast tungsten-based refractory HEA without engineered nanoprecipitates is an appropriate initial state for the proposed comparison.
Stepwise heat treatment or alloying can introduce controllable coherent nanoprecipitates into a refractory HEA.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Efficient dislocation transfer at coherent interfaces delays dislocation pile-up.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve or mitigate stress concentrations.
Relieving stress concentrations postpones premature crack initiation.
The proposed interface-mediated mechanism permits retention of high strength together with improved ductility.
The strength–ductility benefit produced by coherent nanoprecipitates applies under cyclic or high-strain-rate dynamic loading.
The mechanism remains effective from ambient to elevated temperatures as long as the nanoprecipitates remain stable.
Relative to a homogeneous precipitate-free control, the nanoprecipitate-engineered HEA will have higher dynamic yield strength.
Relative to the control, the nanoprecipitate-engineered HEA will exhibit less localized deformation under identical dynamic loading.
Relative to the control, the nanoprecipitate-engineered HEA will exhibit later crack initiation and greater plastic deformation under identical dynamic loading.
The proposed mechanism should generalize from tungsten refractory HEAs to similar multicomponent HEAs in which coherent precipitates can be formed.
The relevant nanoprecipitate size, distribution, and interfacial characteristics required for an optimal strength–ductility balance are not fully established.
Changes in alloy composition may alter the effectiveness of the proposed coherent-interface mechanism.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant ductility improvement together with higher or comparable dynamic yield strength would falsify the hypothesis.
